title: Register for and pay payroll tax
what: Register with the state revenue office and pay payroll tax once wages paid in Australia pass the state's threshold.

sources.title: Payroll Tax Act 2007 (Vic)
sources.publisher: Victorian Legislation (authorised version saved by the owner)
sources.locator: s 86(1) (authorised version 041, saved by the owner)
sources.quote: (1) An employer who is not already registered must apply for registration as an employer under this Act if— (a) during a month the employer pays or is liable to pay, anywhere, wages of more than the weekly threshold amount that are wholly or partly taxable wages; or

confidence_note: Quoted from the authorised PDF the owner saved from the Victorian register (data/raw/vic_legislation/, not committed); the register's documents disallow automated fetching. The regulator's guidance quoted before is kept as a second source.

assessment.summary: A tax on wages above a tax-free threshold. The threshold makes it a tax on growing past a certain size, and exemptions narrow the base; a broad, flat payroll tax would distort less.

marks.reason: The threshold is a tax on growing past it, which can hold firms below it.
Thresholds and exemptions make the tax fall unevenly across employers, distorting hiring and firm size.

assessment.confidence_note: Marks from the register's assessment of the same law (vic-payroll-tax). Evidence on bunching is mixed: e61 found strong bunching at South Australia's threshold; Treasury found little at most states' thresholds before 2015.
